security_controls.control: Discovery returns only the catalogue generated from the exact packaged services. A named tool, prompt or resource request starts its registered local owner and forwards its JSON-RPC payload and response unchanged. The transport does not inspect intent, add case data, send network requests or replay failed calls. Existing service-specific model and external data boundaries still apply.
security_controls.on_violation: Reject unknown targets and return worker failures without replaying possible side effects.

security_controls.control: Concurrent first requests share a worker. Used services retain their review state until the host connection closes; unused services never start during runtime discovery. Closing the connection ends worker input. Separately accepted native jobs retain their existing ownership policy.
security_controls.on_violation: Close the transport on input closure or termination; do not introduce an update-protection companion or retained full-package snapshot.

access.arrangement: The selected host and its authorized local OS account. This transport adds no account or external recipient.

data_returned.content: Existing tool schemas, resource descriptions and prompt definitions, followed by the unchanged selected service response. Requested professional content may enter the selected host model context under the existing workflow contract.

retention.statement: Routing maps, pending requests and child handles live in entry-process memory. The transport adds no case log or persistent output. Existing services retain their existing saved work and technical receipts.

service_details.trigger: The host opens one local entry process per product connection; only explicit tool, prompt or resource use starts its owner. Package builds query discovery in temporary storage with incident delivery disabled.
